หลักฐานของหน่วยงานด้านสิ่งแวดล้อมศิลปกรร: Evidence from cultural environment agencies indicates that the temple was built in 1762 (B.E. 2305) and was originally named Wat “Kongkha”, while the archaeological database of the Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn Anthropology Centre specifies the age of the important historical site from the ordination hall built in 1936 (B.E. 2479). Therefore, the story of its origin should be read as a 2-tier history: the age of the temple according to registration/oral history, versus the age of the building still standing, which are not the same thing.
วัดตั้งอยู่บนที่ราบตะกอนริมคลองตะกั่วป่า: The temple is located on the alluvial plain along Khlong Takua Pa, on the west side of the waterway, in a town with a history as a coastal province and a center for tin mining and maritime trade. Such town context makes the temple likely to have served as a riverside community religious site, but no specific evidence for the temple has been found identifying the builder, the reason for construction, or the direct role of Hokkien Chinese/town governor. Hence, details should not be added beyond the evidence.
อุโบสถที่สร้างใน พ.ศ. 2479 เป็นอาคารก่ออ: The ordination hall built in 1936 (B.E. 2479) is a Southern-style brick and stucco building facing east and adorned with stucco depicting pagodas, Buddha images, dharmachakras, and flora. This reflects its role as both a space for religious ceremonies and a community craftsmanship site from the late Rattanakosin period to the reign of King Rama VIII.
ประวัติวัดที่บันทึกในฐานข้อมูลโบราณคดีระ: The temple history recorded in the archaeological database indicates it was formerly called Wat Kongkha before changing to Wat Kongkha Phimuk in 1940 (B.E. 2483). Meanwhile, the ordination hall and pagoda are still in use, not becoming ruins isolated from the temple. The different names in documents are therefore something that should be preserved to let readers see the place's development.
กรมศิลปากรประกาศขึ้นทะเบียนอุโบสถและเจดี: The Fine Arts Department announced the registration of the ordination hall and pagoda, along with defining the historical site land boundary, in the Royal Gazette on 18 December 1996 (B.E. 2539). The registration ensures the value of the old building is protected as a cultural heritage, while the temple remains a Mahanikaya private temple with residing monks.
ทะเบียนสำนักปฏิบัติธรรมประจำจังหวัดของสำ: The provincial dharma practice center registry of the National Office of Buddhism specifies “Kongkha Phimuk” as the first provincial dharma practice center of Phang Nga, according to the 2002 (B.E. 2545) resolution. Currently, the archaeological database indicates it is maintained and in overall stable condition, but no evidence has been found confirming that the area was affected by the 2004 (B.E. 2547) tsunami or specific years of abandonment/restoration.
ในข้อมูลที่เผยแพร่ล่าสุด วัดคงคาภิมุขยัง: In the latest published information, Wat Kongkha Phimuk still has residing monks and operates as a Mahanikaya private temple. The maintaining entity is identified as the temple itself, with the archaeological database advising to contact Phra Khru Nanthapanyakorn, the abbot, at 076-421-479.
อุโบสถและเจดีย์ยังเป็นโบราณสถานที่ใช้งาน: The ordination hall and pagoda are still active historical sites. Inside, the temple is described as clean, shady, and suitable for religious practices. The temple also serves as the first provincial dharma practice center of Phang Nga, making it a place where people can come to pay respects to Buddha, admire the stucco work, and practice dharma.
กิจกรรมที่มีแหล่งอ้างอิงระบุ ได้แก่ ปฏิบ: Activities with specified references include dharma practice in honor of the monarchy, cross-year chanting, brahmin nun ordination dedicated as royal merit, and summer novice ordination. However, no 2026 announcement has been found confirming the activity schedule, opening-closing times, new restoration projects, or facility details, so it is recommended to call and ask the temple before traveling.
